simulation.note: Monthly steps. Returns are drawn from normal log-returns with the means and volatilities below; inflation varies a little around the chosen scenario. New money goes in by the chosen mix, and the plan is rebalanced to it once a year. One fixed seed, so every plan and scenario runs on the same 500 market paths and the same inputs always give the same fan.
simulation.source: Model choice by the Penny team; not a market assumption.

female.source: Institute for Population and Social Research, Mahidol University (2025). Thai Population Gazette 2025. https://ipsr.mahidol.ac.th/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Gazette2025EN.pdf

male.source: Institute for Population and Social Research, Mahidol University (2025). Thai Population Gazette 2025. https://ipsr.mahidol.ac.th/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Gazette2025EN.pdf

average.source: Computed by the Penny team: the mean of the female and male figures above.

planTo.source: Planning convention used by the Penny team (plan beyond the average, because many people live longer than it).

low.source: Bank of Thailand 2026 headline inflation target range 1–3% (lower bound).

target.source: Bank of Thailand 2026 headline inflation target range 1–3% (midpoint).

high.source: Penny team assumption (not a sourced fact): a scenario above the Bank of Thailand target range. Thai average headline inflation was 6.08% in 2022 (TPSO).

monthlyNoise.source: Model choice by the Penny team: small random variation around the scenario.

cash.label: Cash and deposits
cash.source: Penny team assumption (not a sourced fact): typical Thai savings deposit rates (about 0.5–1.5% a year).

bonds.label: Thai government bonds
bonds.source: Penny team assumption (not a sourced fact): Thai government bond yields (about 2–3% a year).

thaiStocks.label: Thai stocks
thaiStocks.source: Penny team assumption (not a sourced fact): long-run nominal return and volatility of Thai stocks.

globalStocks.label: Global stocks (in US dollars)
globalStocks.source: Penny team assumption (not a sourced fact): long-run nominal return and volatility of broad global equity indices, in US dollars.

stockCorrelation.source: Penny team assumption (not a sourced fact): typical correlation between Thai and global stock returns.

base.source: Penny team assumption (not a sourced fact): THB/USD long-run drift near zero outside crises, about 7% yearly volatility.

weakBaht.source: Penny team scenario: the baht weakens 2% a year against the US dollar. A scenario, not a forecast.

mixes.source: Illustrative mixes by the Penny team for learning; not advice.

1997.label: 1997 Asian financial crisis
1997.hint: Thai stocks fell by about half. The baht lost almost half its value against the US dollar, so savings in US dollars were worth more in baht.
1997.source: SET index 1997 −55% (year-end 831.57 to 372.69, verified). [unverified] Other approximate 1997 changes: baht from about 25 to about 47 per US dollar after the July 1997 float, Thai CPI about 5.6%, US stocks about +31%.

2020.label: 2020 pandemic year
2020.hint: Thai stocks fell a little, global stocks rose and prices dipped slightly.
2020.source: SET index 2020 −8% (year-end 1,579.84 to 1,449.35, verified). [unverified] Other approximate 2020 changes: global stocks about +16%, baht roughly unchanged against the US dollar, Thai CPI about −0.8%.

2022.label: 2022 inflation year
2022.hint: Prices rose fast, about 6% in a year, and global stocks fell by about a fifth.
2022.source: SET index 2022 +1% (year-end 1,657.62 to 1,668.66) and Thai average headline inflation 6.08% (TPSO), verified. [unverified] Global stocks about −18%, baht about 4% weaker against the US dollar.

shocks.note: Economic variables only, applied over 12 months starting at the chosen year. Never a statement about parties, politicians or who governs.
